utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Are there any matters that the parties would like to raise? It seems to me there are none. Could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, the witness is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness move closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please move closer to the microphone, and you can put your headset on -- can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please introduce yourself. What is your first and last name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: My name is Zoran Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, could you please spell your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Z-o-r-a-n R-a-d-o-s-a-v-l-j-e-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Radosavljevic, where and when were you born?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 13th of May, 1957, in the municipality of Loznica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us where the municipality of Loznica is located.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It's in Serbia opposite Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could there be a pause between question and answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you live and what was your education?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I lived and still live in Pilica. I completed my primary school in Pilica, secondary school in Osijek, and further education in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic, could we please pause after my question so that the interpreters can interpret everything we say. Thank you. Where is the village of Pilica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The village of Pilica is 30 kilometres away from Zvornik and 25 kilometres away from Bijeljina and 4 kilometres away from Loznica, which is in the neighbouring republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one point today you said that you completed your secondary school in Osijek.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In Osijek, in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us the reason why you went to school in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I had an aunt there; she still lives in Osijek. And I stayed with her while I was going to secondary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your post -- two-year post secondary education?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The higher administrative school in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you completed the administrative school, did you gain a profession?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was a lawyer specialising in administrative work, and my specialty was misdemeanors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you serve in the army before the outbreak of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. And I did not participate in this war, the last war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This might be a good point to ask you why you didn't serve in the army.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: My right kidney was removed before I was to serve in the army, and the military medical academy found to my eyesight is 65 per cent - that's why I wear glasses - and this is the reason why I did not do my military service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please describe your career up to 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: My first job was in the rubber factory in Zvornik, where I worked from 1984 until 1991. After this when I left the rubber products factory, I worked in Loznica in a privately owned company called Lozane Export. After this I worked in a privately owned company called Milprum [phoen] in Loznica here I worked until 2001. In 2001, in February, I got a job in the ministry or displaced persons and refugees of Republika Srpska, where I remained until the 31st of December, 2003. After this, because our mission was completed - and this was the implementation mission - I was put on stand-by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992 when the war broke out, where were you employed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was employed in Milprum in Loznica, a privately owned company across the street, or rather, seven kilometres away from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is in the Federal Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After I show you a topographical map, could you please show us where the community centre in Pilica is, the Kula primary school in Pilica, and your house. Mr. Radosavljevic, to your right you will see a topographical map, and the scale is 25.000. You have a pointer here. If you can, please indicate with this pointer and assist us by showing us the community centre in Pilica, your house, and the Kula school in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I'll start like this. On my right-hand side is the river Drina. On the left-hand side of the river Drina is the village of Pilica. And here is the Kula primary school. Yes, I found it, it's here. This is Branjevo. Here it is. So this is the Kula primary school, this is river Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please show us, if you can find your way about on this map. Could we please zoom in on this part. Enough. Thank you. Thank you. Could you please tell us now at which crossroads in the village of Pilica is the community centre. Could you point to this.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let me try and find it. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How far from your house is the Kula primary school, if you can point to the primary school now.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The Kula primary school is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see a school marked on this map with the letters S K?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is it from your house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It's three and a half kilometres away from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us where the Branjevo Farm is located?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It's located right here; it's two kilometres away from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is the Pilica community centre from your house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Between my house and the community centre there are three other houses, and the distance is about 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to ask you something else. The Branjevo Farm, is it a military or civilian farm?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: After World War II until this war, the Branjevo Farm was under the Nova Selo/Bijeljina. It is not a military farm. Throughout all this time it was just an agricultural estate. And according to the cadastre it belongs to Zvornik, but it was never run by the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the war broke out, between 1992 and 1995, during the war, what was this farm used for?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: That's where they raised livestock for the army during the war. They kept pigs there, cattle, and this was food for the military during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now ask you the following: How did the local government operate in Pilica after the war? Were you involved in the local government, and can you tell us very briefly how it functioned.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The president of the local commune after the outbreak of hostilities in Pilica was Diko Micic [phoen]. He left for Germany almost immediately. He was succeeded by the president of the commission for wartime conditions, and he was not elected by the people. He was appointed because of the wartime situation. His name was Pero Petrovic. He was the president of the commission, and later he replaced the president of the local commune. And he was at that post until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Pero Petrovic carry out this duty because he was politically active?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was. And he was in the council so they nominated him as a president of the commission for wartime conditions. And when the president left for Germany, we were left without a president and then he took over this duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his political affiliation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He belonged to the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now assist us and remove the map. For the record, this is D128/3. And the scale is 1:25.000. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic, we have had occasion here to listen to the testimony of Pero Petrovic, and he said that throughout the war he was the president of the local commune of Pilica. My question is the following: Was he ever elected as the president of the Pilica local commune?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, he was never elected by the voters. He was the president of the commission. He was a self-appointed president because he was never elected by the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say a "self-appointed president," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I mean the elections were never held at which Pero Petrovic was never elected as president. The people never elected him to that office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm now just briefly going to ask you a few things about 1992. In that year, 1992, in the community centre of Pilica were prisoners brought who were Muslims ethnically?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember where these prisoners came from, where they were brought to the community centre from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I said it was from the Djulici area around Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: At the time, Pero Petrovic, did he perform the duty of the self-appointed president of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you, Mr. Radosavljevic, did you know Dragan Jokic at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know him. I heard of him. And before the war, he was in charge of the village roads, for the construction and reconstruction of roads,, but I never met him personally nor was I ever with him personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that at the beginning of the war he worked in the village on road construction?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we have a roundabout road running for 20 kilometres, and it has to be repaired with machinery two or three times a year. So on that particular occasion he was engaged on the reconstruction of that road. I didn't meet him, but I heard it was Jokic who was repairing the roads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything bad about him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, nothing. I didn't hear anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the war did you have any contacts at all, friendly meetings or anything of the kind with Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. And to the present day I have never been with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Everything you're saying here today, does it have anything to do with your relationship perhaps with Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No reason for that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you yourself, were you militarily involved in 1992 until 1995, Mr. Radosavljevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: For a brief period of time I left up until November, I was just called up. But when I told them that I was not fit for military service, I was exempt. So I was not engaged in any way. I just went once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally have any problems or unpleasantness for not being militarily involved and for not taking up a rifle?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They sent me to sit before a commission to be submitted to a medical examination, and I went in November 1992 to have a re-examination. And they established that I was not fit to do any military service, either during the war or during peacetime either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you something about 1995. Do you remember the events that are linked to the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember the 14th of July. There were rumours going around the village that Srebrenica was to fall and that it would fall. And --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Where were you yourself in the days when Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was at home. I had a work obligation in Loznica. I had to go to work every day, so I was at home basically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "at home," how far is your house away from the community centre or cultural centre at Pilica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I said my house was 100 metres away. I have three -- there are three houses between my own my house and the cultural centre, but we're on the same side, on the right-hand side, looking towards Zvornik. So three houses in between the centre and my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a catering establishment in your house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's been there since 1985.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the catering establishment called? What do people call it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It takes my grandfather's name, and it is called Milakov Han. And in the 1900s my grandfather owned a catering establishment called Han, Milakov, so my father decided to call this catering establishment after him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the proprietor of the establishment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Then and now my mother is the proprietor. She is the owner, and she is in charge of the restaurant, and of late my brother has become involved as well who helps her out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your house and from your catering establishment can you see the entrance into the cultural centre at Pilica?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak up and approach the microphone. We didn't actually hear him say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you again. From your house and catering establishment, can you see the entrance to the cultural centre at Pilica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You can see where you turn to go into the centre, but you can't actually see the entrance and doorway. You can see the entrance into the yard but not the actual entrance to the centre, the building itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm now going to ask you another question, but let me say straight away that we heard certain testimony speaking about another catering establishment which is located opposite the cultural centre. Now my question to you is this: Opposite the cultural centre, is there another catering establishment at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is. It is Novi Zivot. The restaurant is called Novi Zivot, or new life, opposite the cultural centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that restaurant, the Novi Zivot restaurant, can you see the entrance into the cultural centre at Pilica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The cultural centre has three entrances, so I think you can only see one, the first, where the offices are located but not the other two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now to go back to the 14th of July. Were you working on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I worked regularly. When I came back from my job in my mother's restaurant I came across Pero Petrovic and Milovanovic Cviko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take that step by step, Witness. Can you tell us, please, Mr. Radosavljevic, when in the afternoon was this on the 14th, what time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I worked in Loznica from 4.00 to 6.00, or rather, I returned home from 4.00 to 6.00, so I might have come home at 6.00 p.m. actually, round around about that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the name of Cviko Milovanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Cviko Milovanovic was a postman in our village at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the two of them have any reason for being in your mother's catering establishment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were there when I arrived, so I sat down at their table, and whilst talking to them they said that they would like us to go to the elementary school of Kula because something was going on there, somebody had been brought there, so that we should go and have a look to see what had happened and who was -- had been brought there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what context did they say that something was going on there? Actually did Pero say that or did Cviko say that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Pero and Cviko were sitting down together. They were waiting for me to come so that we could all go together to the elementary school, because allegedly they had heard that some people had been brought in there but they didn't know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, Pero told you that he didn't know what it was all about and what was going on?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He didn't know who was brought there, he hadn't received any information, so he wanted us to go off together to see what was happening, because at the time he performed the function of president of the local community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about Cviko Milovanovic, did he occupy any position in the local community?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. He was just the first -- the next-door neighbour, next door to the office, because the postman's office was next to the president of the local community's office at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Pero say why he wanted to go and see what was going on?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He said that he had heard that some war prisoners have been brought there in buses. Now as he didn't have anymore information about that, he wanted us to go off together to see what was happening there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic, on two occasions during this short space of time you said that Pero said he hadn't been informed, that he didn't know, wasn't informed. I wanted to tell you that Pero Petrovic testified here before this Trial Chamber on the 2nd of December, 2003 --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm objecting to this line of questioning simply because -- well, first of all, it seems to be approaching a leading question, but more importantly none of these questions were put to Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Petrovic was never asked any questions relating to the meeting of this witness in cross-examination. And so it actually violates the rule of 90(H)(ii) which states that the case must be put to the witness in cross-examination. The Defence had ample opportunity to do so; Mr. Petrovic was here. They cross-examined him at length, and they never asked him a single question about this meeting. So in the interests of fairness and this rule, I would submit that the Defence not be permitted to continue with these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is surprising argumentation as far as I'm concerned. How could I have asked a question like that of Petrovic, Pero, when I didn't know of the existence of any such meeting? All I can say is that after the statement given by Pero Petrovic here before this Honourable Trial Chamber under oath, that I, together with your investigator, tried to find the relevant evidence to show that he wasn't telling the truth on the occasions. So the arguments we're putting forward today through this witness -- and this witness is here to attempt to state what we knew from the very first day, from day one. Therefore, I had a talk with the present witness after I had talked to Pero Petrovic, and I learned that on that particular day, the 14th, he had -- his movements were quite different to what he set out before this Honourable Trial Chamber here in this courtroom. So I have nothing more to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, I'm a little bit confused with the purpose of your questions to this witness, because we believe that you have to show us the relevance to your client, Mr. Jokic, concerning the testimony of this witness, rather than the challenge to the testimony of another witness. This is the essential issue in this case, that is, it has to be relevant to the whereabouts or his knowledge of these events. If there is no such kind of linkage, I'm afraid those testimonies are somehow irrelevant. Since you just got the information about this meeting, I'll allow you to continue. But you have to bear in mind the warning from the Bench as well as the objections from the Prosecution. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, might I just make a digression, Your Honours. I don't think I need remind you that Petrovic, Pero said that on that day, during his testimony, in the morning hours he talked to the duty operations officer in the Zvornik Brigade from another village, and that he thought it was Dragan Jokic. And that Dragan Jokic informed him about the arrival of the prisoners and said it wasn't his concern and that he could go home. Those were the words he used, Pero Petrovic, used in this courtroom, and they are directly linked to attempts to prove Dragan Jokic's knowledge about the existence of prisoners. But I will move on, Your Honours, and I will of course bear in mind the suggestions and guidelines you have just given me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic, on that day in the afternoon, that is to say the 14th of July, did Pero Petrovic tell you anything at all of his knowledge about the prisoners? Did he mention the fact?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Pero Petrovic wanted us to go to that location together because he didn't know what it was all about. All he had heard was that someone had been brought there. So Cviko and I went with him to the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your conversation with him, did you draw the conclusion that in actual fact he didn't know what this was about at around the -- 6.00 on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He and Cviko were waiting for me to come back from work so that we could drive off in my car to see what was going on. They heard something from someone, but they didn't know any specifics, nothing concrete.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion did Pero Petrovic mention any conversation with Dragan Jokic in the morning hours of the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He didn't say anything. He just said he didn't know what it was all about, but he had just allegedly heard something from a woman but that he knew no specifics about anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did you leave together with Pero and Cviko and go off in the direction of the school at Kula?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. The elementary school of Kula, the three of us. And when we arrived we encountered several buses full of people at different ages. They were being guarded there by soldiers who I had never seen before, nor did I know any of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have the usher's assistance again, please, and show the witness several photographs. For identification purposes, Your Honours, we received them from the Prosecution when Mr. Ruez was questioned, and they are Exhibit Number P17.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic, could you please comment picture by picture as it is placed on the ELMO. Could you please look to the right, to the photograph, and tell us: Is this the Kula school in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the elementary school Kula in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the school you arrived at and in front of which you saw the bus with the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer. It was not recorded in the transcript. Is this the school in front of which you saw the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please take the pointer which is in front of you and show us on the photograph on the ELMO where this road is and where the buses were.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It's impossible to tell from here because it was on the other side. There should be an entrance on the other side. I see several cars here. The road is here where you can see the cars; it's on the upper part. That's where the buses were. It's impossible to tell here because this is the building shown from the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. We will show you another photograph and see if it's possible to see on it what is characteristic about it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: This also shows the Kula building which is just below the school that we had just seen. This is on the opposite side, this road is on the other side. So nothing of this was I able to see on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this school named Kula after this building?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The school is not called Kula. The name of the school is Majolke Brigade. This is where I went to school. The name of the school is Majolke Brigade, the brigades of Majolvica [phoen], not Kula. Kula is a hamlet; it's a part of Pilica that is called that after this building that you are looking at right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic, for the purposes of identification, does that place have anything to do with the location of Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where Kula Grad is.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Kula Grad is in Zvornik. It's above Zvornik. It's the old part of the Zvornik fortress.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move to the next photograph. Do you recognise which part of the Kula school this is.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: This is the part that is inside. This is the entrance used by the teachers. The other side that you showed us a little while ago is the entrance used by the pupils. So it's the entrance from the courtyard used by the pupils, and this here is the official entrance used by the teaching staff. This is where the parking is for the staff cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you throughout the time that you were there in front of the school, was Pero Petrovic with you there all the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Pero came there with me in front of the school and then he went off somewhere. A few minutes later he came back, and he said he had to stay. He had to make tea for somebody; I don't know for whom. And then I went or I left there after some 10 or 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how many buses you saw there.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't count them bus by bus, but I think there were approximately ten buses, not more than then. All the buses were turned in the direction of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will try to show you the last photograph, if you can look at it. The last photograph from this group.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could the usher also take the next photograph and place it on the ELMO, the last photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic, is this the road where the buses were standing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the road where the buses were standing. I saw this part of the elementary school that day when I was there. The two images before were angles of the school that I did not see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many soldiers were guarding this area?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I could tell and count, there were between 20 to 30 soldiers. They were not anybody I knew or had seen before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they wearing white belts?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't able to see that. They were all kinds. Some were wearing the white belts and some were without.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there any comments about why those people were brought there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I thought that there might be an exchange that evening. All the buses were facing in the direction of Zvornik. None were facing in the direction of Bare. So because they were all facing Zvornik, I assumed there would be an exchange that evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Not more than 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I went home and Pero stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Pero tell you the reason why he stayed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He said the soldiers wanted coffee and tea, so he was staying behind in order to help. He was going to make them coffee and tea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is Pero's house from the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It's about the same distance as from my place to the school, about three kilometres. It's up -- it's up to about three kilometres to his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that the road from Pilica, from Zvornik to his house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, his house is halfway from Zvornik and my place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was, let's just clarify it for the transcript, was as follows: Is this road the road that leads to Pero's house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I understood the question. Perhaps I didn't express myself properly. But going from my place towards the elementary school, Pero takes that same road to his house. When you go from my house to Pero's house, the elementary school is halfway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question is: If Pero Petrovic goes to Zvornik, does he have to pass by that school?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the purposes of the transcript could you please repeat your answer to this last question.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Does Pero have to pass by the elementary school if he's going home from work? Yes, he does, unless he takes a shortcut through the woods. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The local community of Pilica in that period, in July, did it have its own premises or offices?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where these offices were.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The office of the local community was right next to the post office, on the left side of the post office, on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is that from the Pilica hall of culture?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: It's in the courtyard of the Dom Kulture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if the office of the local community had a functioning telephone connection and a telephone number in those days?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I know that on the 15th of July sometime between 12.00 and 1.00 a courier came to my courtyard from the local community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, please, let us go step by step. I will be asking you questions about that. My question was: Do you know whether there was a telephone number on the premises of the Pilica local community?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The local community had its telephone and telephone number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now go step by step. Where did you return to on that afternoon of the 14th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: On the 14th I returned home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you spend the night of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I spent it at home with my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice any shooting or anything unusual that night?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't notice anything in particular. Everything was normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you spend the morning of the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I spent it at home because I was working from 2.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any buses passing by with prisoners or any unusual activities in the morning?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't notice anything unusual in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened around noon on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: At about 12.00 or 12.30, a courier came to my office from the local community and said that Pero ordered me to find my rifle and to come and guard these prisoners. Of course I was not a military conscript; I didn't have a gun and I did not wish to take part in this. I took my car. I packed and I crossed over into Serbia, to Loznica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a minute. You said that a courier came?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who it was who came?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Bosko Sukic was the one who came. He is a retired person who before that was a police officer. He came to my yard, and he said that Pero ordered me to find a gun and to come and guard the school or I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said now that you were told that you were supposed to find your rifle?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I didn't have one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could you find a rifle?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, since it was wartime each house had a rifle. I was the one who did not because I was not a military conscript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can Pero Petrovic order you to do anything?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, he could not. But at the time he was the president of the commission for wartime conditions, so he was in authority, in power, so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he take over the organisation relating to securing the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what his intention was, but it was unusual for him to ask me to come and guard the elementary school. I was not a military conscript, and I felt that I was not obliged to do anything like that, and that is why I went to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this courier mention any connection between Pero Petrovic and Dragan Jokic to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't discuss anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the courier tell you where Pero Petrovic was at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: He didn't say anything, actually. He just said that I should go to his office and that I would receive my assignment there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we're going back to the question of when you say "to go to his office," which office were you thinking of?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: There was an office next to the post office where the president of the local community was located. All the activities, all his duties, were performed from that -- conducting from that office. So that is about 100 metres away from where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am now going to ask the Prosecution to help us in a technical aspect. We would like to show you Prosecution Exhibit 9.10, which is actually a short videoclip of the cultural centre in Pilica so that we can ask this witness to identify, if possible, where this office was and where the cultural centre was. I would like to thank Ms. Janet, who is assisting us in the technical aspect of showing this exhibit to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic, I would like to ask you if you can to give us your comments, and if you need the clip to be stopped anywhere, just say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what this is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the road. You have just passed my house. And we need to stop here, please. Can you stop here. Perhaps we can go a little bit ahead, past the monument, and then straight ahead we would be able to see Pero's office the time. Yes, this is the cultural centre. Yes, can you go a little bit further so that we see the other monument which is right after this one. This is good. You can -- can you go back a little bit so we can see the right-hand corner, because right here where this young man is sitting, the office is to the right of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this shot, could you also see the entrance to your house and the entrance to your yard?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You passed my yard and my house. The restaurant is on the right-hand side. Going towards the cultural centre is the restaurant of my mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we see this young man sitting on this fence here.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please show us now where the -- or rather, how far from this place are the premises of the local community?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: To the right from this young man sitting on the fence, if you follow along the wall, you can see the office of Pero Petrovic straight ahead. And only the post office is next to it. After the -- behind the fence you can see the cement path that leads to the office of Pero Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask the usher to help us with the paragraph showing the entrance to the Pilica cultural centre. The Prosecution has this photograph. For purposes of identification, this is P19.3, admitted into evidence during the testimony of Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Radosavljevic, could you please comment on the location of the entrance to the centre and where Pero Petrovic's office is.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Going through this entrance, through this doorway, you come straight to the door of Pero Petrovic's office. Where the pointer is now is where the office of the local commune used to be. And this used to be the entrance to the pre-war office. If you go through here and through the hallway, you come straight to Pero Petrovic's door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What did you do after you were informed that you were supposed to report to Pero Petrovic in his office in order to be given an assignment to guard the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I got into my car and went to my work in Loznica. From there I called my wife and told her to get the children and pack some things. And we went to Vrnjacka Banja, 300 kilometres away from that place. All the time I was in office. It was at Sepacki Put number 17. I was in telephone contact with my wife Ranka [phoen] telling her to pack, to take this, to take that, not forget to take money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What as the reason you decided to leave Bosnia, cross over into Serbia and go to Banja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I was not -- or I had not been active in the military. As Pero had told me to find a rifle and to come and guard the camp, I didn't want to get blood on my hands. I was afraid I might become a war criminal myself. And as I had managed to stay out of that up to that point, I wanted to go on like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on the 15th of July you contacted your wife several times?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was working in a trading company in Loznica. And from there I called my wife several times reminding her what things she had to take, telling her to take the children. I told her we would not be back home for some time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you communicate by telephone?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your restaurant and in your flat did you have a telephone?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We always had a phone. I got my first telephone in 1988, and I've always had a telephone since then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout these days from the 10th to the end of July, were telephone communications in good order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, unless there was a power shortage. And then there would be a short interruption.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher assist us now and show the witness D116/3, which is information concerning the operation of telephone lines in this period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic, according to this certificate obtained by the Defence through Ozrenka Jaksic, the telecom of Republika Srpska informs us that in 1995 the local community office of Pilica used the following telephone number: 590054. And this number was functional in the month of July 1995. Have you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does this confirm what you say, that in July 1995 telephones were fully operational throughout?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As I've told you, I called my wife on several occasions. I often spoke to my wife while I was working in Loznica. I called home. Pilica had 200 telephone numbers at the time in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now read to you an excerpt from the transcript of the testimony of Pero Petrovic and his statement before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For purposes of identification, Your Honour, this is an excerpt from the transcript, page 5553 in English. And this is the cross-examination conducted by me of Pero Petrovic on the 3rd of December, 2003.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic, will you please follow what I'm saying. I asked Pero Petrovic the following. He was saying that on the 14th of July he went to Sepuk to call the command of the Zvornik Brigade and to talk to the brigade duty officer. He thought it was Jokic. And I asked him why he went from Pilica to Sepuk to conduct this telephone conversation. And his reply was: "There was no telephone in Pilica, but I can't remember." My next question was: "Sorry. I don't understand you. You cannot remember whether it worked or not?" The answer given by Petrovic was: "I'm not aware of the reason why it didn't work. I know we went to Sepuk because it was impossible to phone from Pilica. But I don't know the reason why the lines were down. We often went to the post office there during the war because the lines were often down during the war. And this is what I had in mind when I declared in my statement that the telephone was not working." What I want to ask you again, Mr. Radosavljevic, is: Are you certain that during those days, the 14th and 15th of July, 1995, the telephones were in good working order in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure about that day, yes. The lines may have been down the day before or the day after, but I'm absolutely certain that on the 15th the telephones were working. I called my relative. I called him home -- I called home to talk to my wife to tell her what things to take, to explain to her that we were leaving Pilica for a longer period of time. So it wasn't just once that I called her. I called her again and again on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And my next question is: On the 14th of July from your office did you call home?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: We all worked in offices and we were in the habit of calling home. I was in the habit of calling home every day, and I still do. I call my family every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that the telephones were operational?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I will conclude with another part of this statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, before you turn to other subjects, could I ask: Do you know who does this number 590054 belong to in that document? In that document the certification from the - I think - post office says the telephone number 590054 was functional in the month of July 1995. Who does this number belong to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, according to the post office report, the telecom of Republika Srpska, this is the telephone number of the local office of the Pilica local commune. And this telephone was in the offices, in the office of the Pilica local commune.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic, I will read to you another excerpt from the questions I put to Mr. Petrovic on that occasion. This is page 5554, and this is the cross-examination of the 3rd of December, 1995 [as interpreted], line 11. I said: "Do you know where Milijan's cafe is located in relation to your office?" The witness responded: "Yes. On the road towards Bijeljina, some 100 metres away down the road. "How far from your office is Jovanovic's [phoen] house in Sepuk?" And he said: "Three to four kilometres, maybe more." Do you know at that time there was a telephone in Milijan's cafe. He said: "I can't remember. I know there was a phone, but I'm not sure if the phone was working. There had been a phone before the war; I know that." My question is: When you say "Milijan's cafe," does this referring to your mother's establishment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was better known by my father's name than my mother's name. They called it Milijan's cafe. The didn't call it Ivanka's cafe most often, although my mother was running it..

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your father's name Milan?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this answer correct that your cafe was 100 metres down the road?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said. It's about 100 metres away from the office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you try to respond once again to the following question: Throughout this time was there a telephone line?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I repeat again, on the 14th and the 15th the telephone was working. The lines would be down if it rained because then there would be a power shortage. So the batteries had to be filled again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have about 10 minutes to go, and I think that this may be a use -- a convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll take a break and we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, let's resume the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic, we left off when I showed you excerpts from the transcript of the cross-examination of Mr. Pero Petrovic. You permanent that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just going to put another excerpt to you, and then that would round off that area. I asked Pero Petrovic, who was the witness, the following thing: "Would you agree with me when I say that it is logical that you went to Milijan's cafe that day which is 100 metres away to telephone to check what he told you instead of going to Sepuk to have that conversation?" And the witness's answer was: "Yes, I agree. That would be more logical. But perhaps at that time I knew the fact that in Milijan's cafe the telephone wasn't working. Perhaps I wasn't quite sure. Perhaps I decided to go because the telephone wasn't working that day. I mean, I didn't have information, exact information, as to which telephone in which household was working on that particular day." And then I go on to say: "I don't rule out the possibility that on that day it was working as well."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, that passage and excerpt is to be found on page 5555, line 7 to 15. And the date is the 3rd of December, 2003.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Petrovic says at one point that it was possible that the telephone worked in my offices, he says. And my question was this, or rather, my question is this to you now: What Pero Petrovic said, the place he went to telephone which was Donji Sepuk, was it also somewhere where the telephones were working sometimes but not other times because of the battery?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They all work according to the same principle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I wanted to hear from you as an answer. And now I'll draw my examination to a close for today. When did you go back to Pilica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I went back 16 or 17 days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that in the meantime crimes had been committed at the Branjevo Farm?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I heard -- I talked to from father from Vrnjacka Banja so I was kept abreast of the situation. And I did not go back until I was told that everything was back to normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came home, were you informed that the crime had been committed there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you happen to hear that Dragan Jokic was involved in any of those events at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Radosavljevic. I have no further questions for you. If there are any other questions, would you please answer them. If Mr. Karnavas has any questions for you or the Prosecution or Their Honours. Thank you once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Karnavas, do you have any questions to put to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. Good morning, sir. I have no questions for the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination? Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Your Honours. I think I have just a couple of questions, just a very short cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please. Cross-examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Now, sir, I want to go back to the beginning of your testimony where you indicated that the Branjevo Farm, according to you, was not a military farm. And I'd like to refer to Exhibit 873, I believe. If we can put the English translation on the ELMO. Thank you. Now, if we look at this article, sir, it's from the from the Drinski magazine dated June of 1995. And it refers to the military farm. And I can read a few excerpts from that and I'll ask you about that. The -- it starts off with indicating that Milan Stojanovic 's unit produces for itself large quantities of potatoes, onions, tomatoes tobacco, peas, green beans and other vegetables. It states: "The war has been going on for a long time and we do not know when it will end. That is why we have to be as well organised as possible in every respect, and especially in organising food supplies. In view of our potential in terms of agriculture, we should have no problem in feeding the army and the people, said officer Milan Stojanovic at the beginning of our discussion of the military farm." And it goes on. And at the very bottom of the first page there is a reference to the director Tomo Simic, it says: "Who told us a few things about the cooperation of the army and this company." On the next page he's quoted as saying: "We help each other out. There is a moral and financial obligation to help the army." And it continues. So according to this article, sir, the Branjevo Farm was in fact a military farm. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I said a moment ago that Branjevo was never a military farm up until the war. In wartime they did produce food for the army. So before that it was never a military farm. When the war broke out, this farm produced and grew food for the army but not before or after. And after the war now it's not a military farm either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: If that answers your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to clarify one other point, sir. This won't take long. You indicated that you were home on the night of the 14th of July. Is that right? You were home during that evening?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't hear any shooting that may have been coming from the Pilica school at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear any shooting, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions out of the cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Just a few questions. Re-examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Radosavljevic, would you take a look at that same exhibit we were looking at a moment ago. And in paragraph 3 it says: "In considering the fact that in the area of responsibility of this unit you find the Branjevo Farm, we came up of the idea of taking part of the land and using it for the -- for army purposes. The Agropro management gave the land to the army." Have you had a chance to read through that passage?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, does that paragraph in the Drinski newspaper confirm your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does. It does confirm it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more question. Do you know who Milan Stanojevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Milan Stanojevic was the commander of that battalion that in was there, that was in charge there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this farm, is it located within the area of the responsibility of the Milan Stanojevic battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage are there any documents to tender? Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. With your permission we should like to tender into evidence Defence Exhibit D116/3, which is the certificate from telecom Republika Srpska, and D69.1/3; D69.5/3, that is the five photographs that we showed the witness today. And it refer -- they refer to the Kula school, which by mistake was registered as Prosecution Exhibit P19 -- 17/2 because it was a different photograph. That wasn't the photograph we showed the witness but the building and the facility is the same. So it is D69.1/3 up until D69.5/3. The set of five photographs depicting the school. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Those documents are admitted into evidence. On the part of the Prosecution, do you have any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We would like to tender P873 which is the Drinski magazine or passage that we read from, along with the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for this document, we don't see any differences between the testimony of this witness and what is said in that document. And most parts are read in the transcript, so we doubt very much whether it's still a necessity to admit that piece of the information into the evidence at this stage. Ms. Issa, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I would only perhaps refer to the second paragraph of the document. That may be a slight variation to what the witness has told us. And I would submit that it would be best to simply admit it, to put the whole testimony into context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Since there is -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you recall, when we proposed that the Slobodna Bosna article be tendered as well we said that both the Prosecution and ourselves quoted the relevant passages from that newspaper article, so the situation is the same here. Both the Prosecutor and I myself quoted this portion, which is the relevant portion for both sides. And I think that is sufficient for the transcript because I see no difference between the testimony and what was noted here, although in principle we don't have anything against having the whole article tendered into evidence. We don't consider that there is any difference, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, on this very issue I sense a difference between the parties, because the Prosecution claims there is a slight difference but the Defence believes there's no difference at all. So in this situation we admit this document into the evidence. It is so decided. Well, Witness, thank you very much indeed for coming to The Hague to give your testimony. Madam Usher will show you out of the room. We wish you a pleasant journey back home. You may leave now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, would you please brief us on the situation of the witnesses for this week.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we have planned another witness for today. We think the witness has arrived and that his testimony will be relatively brief. It speaks to the character of our client, Dragan Jokic. The witness for tomorrow still hasn't received his travelling papers, and in the course of the day we shall be able to inform the Court whether everything is in order or whether we'll have to give up hearing that witness's testimony. (Redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: (Redacted)And on Thursday we have military expert Dragoslav Lackovic, and we'll try and abide by your proposal of having his statement given under 94 bis. So that is an issue we will solve today and we shall be informing you of our decision by the end of the day so we have a witness for Friday as well. He will be coming in on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And could we have the next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please stand up and make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you hear me, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you introduce yourself, please, what your name is, your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: I apologise, but do I have to get up?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. You can remain seated.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: I name is Mirko Rebic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record will you please spell your name letter by letter, your first and last name?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: M-i-r-k-o R-e-b-i-c.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rebic. Would you now tell us when and where you were born.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 19th of September, 1953, in Baljkovica, the Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what education you've had and what jobs you have held. Where did you complete elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: I completed elementary school, or rather, four years of primary school in my native village of Baljkovica. And then I went to eight years of elementary school in Zvornik and secondary school, the gymnasium, I graduated in Zvornik. After secondary school I enrolled in the university of Novi Sad at the faculty of law. And I graduated from the faculty of law at the end of 1978 and the beginning of 1979.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you continued with your high school education, did you travel from your village or did you live in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: I travelled also during the period when I went to elementary school. And then I continued for the most part to do the same when I attended the gymnasium. The transportation wasn't so well developed, I'm talking about bus transport. So for those of us who wanted to go to school, we had to walk there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where Novi Sad is.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: Novi Sad is the administrative centre of the autonomous province of Vojvodina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that part of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: Administratively speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you graduated from university, what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: After I graduated my first job was in the organs of the Municipal Assembly of Zvornik; however, I didn't stay there for very long. I transferred to the business sector. For a while I worked in a construction company, in Engineering Zvornik, after which I moved Jadar timber industry factory where I worked until 1992. After that I continued to work there for some periods up until the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Allow me to stop you there for just a moment. In 1992 what was your job in the Jadar Zvornik company?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: Since I completed the faculty of law, I worked as the manager of the legal and personnel sector of that company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once the war broke out in the area of the Zvornik municipality, were you mobilised? Did you join the army?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: When the unfortunate events in 1992 began to play out, I was mobilised as early as May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe this is a good point to ask you whether by that time you had served in the military and did you have any ranks.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: I had served my regular military term after I graduated from university; that was the order of things. I did serve in the Yugoslav People's Army. And I had the rank of lance corporal but that was because of the work that I was doing in the military. Because I worked with the commander for morale and political affairs, and the person who performed that job had to have that rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After you were mobilised and joined the Army of Republika Srpska, can you remember which unit you were deployed to.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: I must say that the first call-up in May 1992 did not take so long because I was needed in my company where I was already employed. There was another mobilisation in early 1993 when I was assigned to an infantry battalion which changed its name often. At the time when I was in it, it was called the 4th Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps this would be a good time to say --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: This battalion was located in Drinjaca. That's where the command was. This is from the Drina River upstream towards Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: For the most part during the time that I was in the battalion, Mr. Radika Petrovic was the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rebic, did you carry out any military duties? Did you have any ranks or specific position in the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: No. Throughout the time that I was mobilised I didn't occupy any command post, and I didn't have any rank. Most of the time that I was there, I was in the so-called communications unit. We made sure that the lines were functioning from the command to the trenches and the other way. So that was my main task, together with the other men who were in that company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in this battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: I think that that was until the end of 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go at the end of 1994? Did you leave the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: In 1994 when I was released, demobilised, I was sent for work duty back to my company, Jadar. This is where I worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your job at the time in Jadar?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: The same as before. I was manager of the legal and personnel sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you on work duty in Jadar? Did you return to the army before the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: After I was demobilised, I no longer returned to the army. But sometime before the end of 1995 following the signing of the Dayton Peace Accords under a decision of the president of the municipality at the time, I was allocated to the commission for refugee affairs. In view of the events at the time and the fact that a large number of population left Sarajevo, many of them came to the territory of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you work on this assignment?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: I worked on this assignment until April the following year. This is 1996. Sometime until late May or early April at a meeting of the Municipal Assembly of Zvornik, I was elected as president of the Executive Board or the president of the local government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you at the post of president of the municipal government of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: I remained at that post until October or November 1997. There were local elections in the territory of Republika Srpska, including Zvornik naturally. And after the elections, I was the president of the Municipal Assembly of Zvornik. I stayed at that post until the end of 1998. After the republican authority was taken over by the Sloga coalition, this also encompassed the local authorities, whereby I was no longer the president of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that from April 1996 until the end of 1998 you were carrying out the most important functions in the municipality of Zvornik in the political sense?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, in the political sense, but also in other ways. I don't know exactly how to express that. This was a local government, local authority. And the position of the president of the municipality is the number one post in the territory of a sociopolitical community like a municipality, or as it is called in the west it would correspond to the post of mayor in the western system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what have you been doing since then until now? Are you employed at all?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: After I stopped being the president of the municipality, after a short period, I started work as the director of a textile factory where I stayed until 2002. Following the privatisation which was implemented in that area and the way that it was implemented, I was no longer in that factory and I did not keep the post that I was carrying out. So since that time until now, I have not been working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question, Mr. Rebic, are you married? Do you have children?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO REBIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am married. I'm the father of two children. I have a daughter and a son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
